notes: TRULY AMBIGUOUS: '03/04/2023' could mean March 4 (US/MM-DD) or April 3 (DD-MM) with no way to tell from the string alone. This codebase's documented, existing convention is MM/DD-first (see normalize.parse_date's docstring) -- so March 4 is the CORRECT/expected result here, unchanged by the DD/MM fix below. Included specifically to prove the fix (which only kicks in when MM/DD is INVALID, e.g. fixture 16) doesn't also flip this already-correct, merely-ambiguous case.
